hooks.name: Scaffold a new decay policy

action.prompt:
GATE (check this first): this hook runs on every prompt. Read the user's prompt (the USER_PROMPT environment variable, or the message itself). If it does NOT explicitly ask you to scaffold a decay policy for a named app, do nothing at all: create no files, write no log entry, and do not mention this hook or this gate. Only if it does, continue below.

Scaffold a new decay policy for the app named in the prompt (ask if none is given).
Create, under apps/<app-name>/src/:
1. policy.ts implementing the DecayPolicy contract exactly as defined in the "Type Contract" section of .kiro/specs/engine/requirements.md. Do not invent other signatures. Every function body is a TODO: decay rules belong to the developer (see .kiro/steering/authorship.md). Do not write them.
2. skin.css with CSS variables (--bg, --panel, --line, --text, --dim, --acc, --good, --warn, --bad), taking the values from the app's section of .kiro/steering/design-tokens.md where one exists, and a comment naming the app's metaphor from .kiro/steering/theme-and-wording.md.
3. policy.test.ts with test stubs written as `it.todo(...)`, never as empty passing tests (see .kiro/steering/no-fake-tests.md): health stays 0-100, same input gives same output, healthAt never increases between events, the policy passes checkPolicy, and one outcome test ("dies on day N if never tended").
4. If apps/<app-name>/package.json or tsconfig.json is missing, create minimal ones modelled on apps/study-dungeon (name @decay-engine/<app-name>, engine as a workspace dependency, vitest and typescript as dev dependencies, scripts test and typecheck). No React or Vite yet.
Do not modify packages/engine. Log this in docs/KIRO_LOG.md as a new session, naming this hook as the trigger.

hooks.description: Creates the starting files for a new app's decay policy, skin and tests. Runs on every prompt but acts only when the prompt asks for a scaffold (the matcher field is not documented for prompt hooks, so the gate is in the instructions).
